# Entanglement Assistance Output Limits

> Input and output dimension laws for the classical communication advantage of unlimited preshared entanglement through finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channels.

## Scientific question and result

For a channel T:A→B, write a=dim A, b=rank T(I_A) for its effective output dimension, and r for the real affine dimension of its output-state image. The joint estimate is C_E(T)≤(√[2(e−1)min{2r,4a−3}]+√b)² χ(T). For 2≤b≤a, the largest possible gain C_E/C has order min{a,b²−1}. Arbitrary finite input dimensions and arbitrarily small output eigenvalues remain covered by the output bound. The weak-signal version gives the matching joint order at all aspect ratios around a fixed full-rank replacer.

## Distinctions to preserve

- C(T) is the regularized ordinary classical capacity. Do not replace it by the single-use Holevo quantity χ(T) for an arbitrary channel; the proof uses χ(T)≤C(T).
- C_E(T) allows unlimited preshared entanglement. The dimension b counts the channel output alone, not the receiver's stored entanglement or the reference system.
- The global converse covers every finite channel dimension. Matching order for arbitrary channels holds when b≤a, and over any fixed comparable-dimension range. The matching local law assumes a fixed full-rank replacer and takes the signal to zero at fixed dimensions.
- Use the capacity inequality when C(T)=0. A ratio is only defined when the denominator is positive.
- The BKM metric is evaluated on the effective support and, for Schmidt decompositions, on the support of the input marginal. The compressed square (PHP)² and the compression PH²P need not coincide.
- A genuine fixed-input-basis classical stochastic channel has no entanglement-assisted gain. Classical output alone does not imply this; the trine measurement example has a gain.
- Fixed output dimension with weak depolarizing signal and growing output dimension at the negative complete-positivity boundary are different limits. The latter has ratio 2b+4/3−4/(9b)+O(b⁻²).
- Quadratic order in b is optimal even for entanglement-breaking channels with a proportional to b². Linear order is optimal for commuting output images. The weak-signal witnesses have vanishing absolute rates in the limit.
- At a maximally mixed replacer, the local coefficient is at most min{r,k+1} for a Schmidt-rank-k input. Exact saturation at r≥2 forces Clifford observables and Schmidt rank at least 2^floor(r/2). This rank concerns a single-use optimizing purification.
- Finite computations check calculations and conventions. The analytical proof establishes the general result.
